body_table: Maps 9 player form IDs to spriteset and sprite tile data locations. Each 6-byte body-entry: { Address spriteset_ptr, @Binary sprite_tiles_ptr }. Forms: Will (normal), Freedan, Shadow, Shadow alt, Will alt, Ability FX, Will FX, Shadow FX, Shadow mode. Referenced by sprite_composition.asm (spriteset/tile DMA source) and actor_execution.asm (form transitions).
character_name_table: Pointer table of character display names: Will, Kara, Lance, Erik, Seth, and other story characters. Used in dialog and status screens.
consolestring_01D9D8: 3 fixed ConsoleString entries displayed at boot: region lockout warning ('This game pak is not designed for your SUPER FAMICOM...'), 'PUSH START BUTTON', and copyright notice ('© 1994 QUINTET/ENIX, MARIKO OHARA/MOTO HAGIO, YASUHIRO KAWASAKI, LICENSED TO NINTENDO').
cosine_table_16bit: 16-bit high-precision cosine table — 128 word entries covering one quarter-wave. Values range $7FFF (1.0) down to $0000 (0.0) (its entries are also the falling quarter, 90°–180°, of the sine cycle read from sine_table_16bit). Paired with sine_table_16bit for Mode 7 matrix computations in mode7_perspective.asm, which indexes it up to 512 words so the read continues through neg_sine_halfwave_16bit and cosine_table_16bit_tail.
cosine_table_16bit_tail: Copy of sine_table_16bit's 128 words (the rising quarter; entries $00–$09 and $70–$7F spot-checked identical). It follows neg_sine_halfwave_16bit so that the 512-word cosine cycle read from cosine_table_16bit ends with the 270°–360° quarter — it is not a spare duplicate. No code names it directly.
dialog_dictionary_a: First dialog text dictionary — pointer table of commonly used words/phrases for text compression. Control code $D6 DictionaryA reads a 1-byte index and recursively renders the string. Contains the most frequently used words (the, you, have, etc.). Part of IOG's dual-dictionary compression giving ~512 compressed word slots.
dialog_dictionary_b: Second dialog text dictionary — extended word list for less frequently used words and longer phrases. Triggered by control code $D7 DictionaryB. Functions identically to dictionary A but covers the second 256-word bank.
dialog_template_table: 22 reusable dialog box templates ($00–$15) invoked by the $C2 InsertTemplate control code. Templates $00–$07: screen-effect presets with [SEP] palette shifts and [SFX] sound triggers for Dark Space transformations. Templates $08–$11: dialog box size presets with [DLG] position and [SIZ] line-count configuration. Template $12: 'Where do you go?' world map prompt. Templates $13–$15: silent screen-effect variants. Referenced by DialogStringRenderer.asm InsertTemplate handler.
direction_velocity_table: Maps 9 cardinal/diagonal directions to sprite frame and velocity parameters. Each 2-byte direction-velocity entry: byte 0 = base animation frame for that direction, byte 1 = movement speed. Entries cover S, N, E, W, SE, SW, idle variants, and NE/NW. Referenced by actor_execution.asm (actor facing) and forced_walk.asm (forced movement velocity per direction).
display_preset_table: Index table of 47 display preset configurations ($00–$2E). Each 10-byte display-preset struct defines PPU register values for a scene's graphics mode: BG mode/tile size, tilemap bases, screen designation, color math/window masks, scroll config, and special flags. The scene loader selects a preset index from scene metadata and configures all PPU registers accordingly. Every playable area in the game references one of these presets.
enemy_clear_reward_table: Maps each scene ID ($00–$FF) to its enemy-clear reward tier: $00 = no reward, $01–$03 = reward tiers (minor/medium/major stat boosts or items). When all enemies in a Dark Space room are defeated, this table determines what reward the player receives. Central to IOG's stat progression. Referenced by StandardEnemyDefeatHandler (on last enemy kill), field_reveal_object (reveals reward), and radar_map_screen (draws chest icons for rewarded scenes).
enemy_stats_table: Master enemy stat table — 110 entries of 4-byte enemy-stats structs indexed by enemy type ID. Fields: HP (0=$00 non-combat, $7F/$FF = boss-tier), ATK (attack power), DEF ($7F = immune to normal damage), Type (0–3, affects damage calculations). Boss actors often reference specific offsets directly. The combat system reads these values for all damage calculations.
event_block_table: 158 entries of 8-byte event-block-def structs defining event-triggered tile copy operations. Fields: scene ID, source X/Y tile, width, height, dest X/Y tile, layer flag. Used for doors opening/closing, barriers appearing/disappearing, puzzle state changes. LookupEventBlock validates scene ID before execution (an entry whose scene differs from sceneCurrent is skipped); the rectangle is copied from the source to the destination coordinates. Coordinates and sizes are in 16×16 metatiles. Indexed by event_index × 8; the index comes from the COP event-block commands, an enemy's scene-record event byte (actor_execution) or an actor's deathActionIdx. Entry $07 is an all-zero 1×1 placeholder (scene 0); entries $06, $14 and $20 target layer 1 (layer flag 1), all others layer 0.
forced_walk_sequence_table: Table of 16 pointers ($00–$0F) to forced-walk animation frame sequences. Each sequence is a stream of paired bytes (sprite frame index + movement step delta), terminated by $00,$00. Used during cutscene character movement to define step patterns — selecting walking animation frames and controlling movement speed per tick. Referenced exclusively by forced_walk.asm, indexed by direction.
freedan_ability_anim_table: Animation configuration for Freedan's 3 attack abilities. Same structure as will_ability_anim_table. Index 0 = Dark Friar, 1 = Aura Barrier, 2 = Earthquaker. Referenced by LoadAbilityAnimTableB in attack_ability_system.asm.
hdma_channel_config: DMAP transfer mode for each PPU B-bus register — 64 byte entries indexed by the register's low byte ($2100 + index; the HDMA COP ops pass that byte, e.g. #0F = BG2HOFS, #26 = WH0). The low 3 bits are the DMAP transfer mode: 0 = one register, 1 = two registers (p, p+1), 2 = one register written twice. Matches the PPU map: 2 for the scroll registers $0D–$14, the mode 7 registers $1B–$20 and CGDATA $22, 1 for the VRAM address/data pairs $16–$19 and the window pairs $26–$29. The indirect-HDMA flag ($40) is not stored here; SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect and QueueHdmaChannel OR it in. Entries $34–$3F cover the read-only PPU registers (MPY, SLHV, OAMDATAREAD, VMDATAREAD, CGDATAREAD, OPHCT/OPVCT, STAT77/78) and carry bit 7 ($80/$81/$82), the DMAP PPU-to-CPU direction bit. Referenced by SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect/Direct in hdma_dma_spc.asm, QueueHdmaChannel in cop_handlers_hdma_dma.asm, and scanline_band_hdma_thinker.asm (which masks with AND #$07).
item_description_table: Pointer table of detailed item help text strings displayed on the item selection screen. Provides multi-line descriptions of each item's function and lore.
item_get_dialog_table: Maps item IDs to acquisition dialog strings ('Will got a Red Jewel!', 'HP increased by 1!', etc.). Includes formulaic stat-increase strings, unique key item messages, shared Mystic Statue strings, inventory-full messages, and 'nothing found' defaults. Referenced by inventory_mgmt.asm and combat_collision.asm.
item_menu_table: Pointer table of 64 item menu descriptions — longer text shown when hovering over items in the inventory menu. Each entry provides a one-line functional description of the item's purpose.
item_name_table: Pointer table of 64 item display names used in inventory screens and item acquisition dialogs. Entries include: Red Jewel, Herb, Incan Statue A/B, Crystal Ball, Wind Melody, Lola's Melody, Mine Key A/B, Memory Melody, Elevator Key, Palace Key, Purify Stone, Rama Statue, Magic Dust, Black Glasses, Gorgon Flower, Hieroglyphs, Aura, Crystal Ring, etc. Blank entries ($2A–$38) are unused slots. Entries $39–$3F are 'Mystic Statue' variants.
non_discardable_item_bits: 8-byte binary separator between the item menu table and item description table. Padding/alignment data.
misc_ui_strings: Pointer table of miscellaneous UI strings: status labels, menu headers, save/load prompts, game over text, and other system messages.
movement_delta_table: Largest table in bank 1 (~5 KB). Contains 85 pointers ($00–$54) to pre-computed movement delta sequences as delta-node linked lists. Each delta-node: { Word value, &delta-node next }. Value = signed 16-bit per-frame movement delta. Self-referencing next = hold constant. Simple entries ($00–$11) are single constants; complex entries ($12+) trace velocity curves (acceleration ramps, arcs, deceleration). Used by WorldMapController (travel animation), forced_walk/hit_stagger (knockback), and camera scrolling.
music_pointer_array: 30 long-pointer entries covering 27 distinct BGM tracks (bgm_lively_city appears 4 times, at entries $00, $01, $0C, $16). Entry index = music ID - 1, so entry $1B (bgm_lively_city_by_the_sea) is music ID $1C, which matches the `music < #1C, ... @bgm_lively_city_by_the_sea >` scene records. The repeated lively_city entries sit at IDs $01, $02, $0D and $17; IDs $0D/$17 look like placeholders for unused IDs (inferred). The no-music track is entry $1A (ID $1B). Referenced by hdma_dma_spc.asm: LoadMusicFromTransitionState computes musicTransitionState x 3, reads the entry at `table-3 + index` into $46/$47 and the `srcCacheMusic` shadow ($0687/$0688), then calls SpcBlockTransfer.
neg_sine_halfwave_16bit: Negated half-wave 16-bit sine — 256 word entries, entry k ≈ −32767 × sin(k × 0.703125°): $0000 at k=0, trough $8001 at k=$80, back to $FE6E (−402) at k=$FF; never positive. It supplies angles 180°–360° of the 512-word sine cycle that follows sine_table_16bit and cosine_table_16bit, and the 90°–270° part of the cosine cycle read from cosine_table_16bit. Reached only by running past the end of those tables (mode7_perspective index up to 511); no code names it directly.
parallax_scroll_table: 37 entry pointers (word table, bank 01) indexed by the scanline_band_hdma_thinker spawn parameter. See the block note.
hdma_entry_stride_by_mode: HDMA entry stride (count byte + data bytes) indexed by the DMAP transfer mode: mode 0 = 2, modes 1 and 2 = 3. ParallaxResolveEntryStride (scanline_band_hdma_thinker) looks up hdma_channel_config[register index] & 7 and stores the result in DP $04, where the band writers use it to step the buffer write pointer. It is a stride, not a scroll speed. Only entries 00-02 ($02, $03, $03) are reachable because every config byte has a low-3-bit value of 0-2; entries 03-0C ($05, $05, $64, $00, then $FF / $7F pairs) have no reader (the FF 7F pattern resembles HDMA line-count data, inferred).
ramp_curve_arc_32: Entry 1 of ramp_motion_curves: 32 signed Y deltas in pixels, -8 at the start, 0 at frames 15-17 and +8 at the end. Cumulative rise peaks at -50 (up) at frame 14; the sum is +8, so the player lands 8 pixels lower. Used by all other east/west ramps (spawn type 3).
ramp_curve_arc_64: Entry 0 of ramp_motion_curves: 64 signed Y deltas in pixels, one per frame, -16 at the start, 0 around frames 29-36 and +16 at the end. Cumulative rise peaks at -204 (up) at frame 28; the sum is 0. Used by the Itory ramp pair (spawn type 1).
ramp_motion_curves: Two arc entries (3 bytes each: curve address, frame count) used by RampArcDriver in ramps.asm. The ramp's arc child reads the player's statsPtr (0 or 1, set from the ramp's spawn type byte) x 3, then adds one sign-extended curve byte per frame to the PLAYER's Y ($16, confirmed: the child's $04 link is the spawner, the player). Values are pixel deltas. Entry 0: 64 frames, rises up to 204 pixels (frame 28) and returns, net 0. Entry 1: 32 frames, rises up to 50 pixels (frame 14), net +8 (ends 8 pixels lower). Both curves repeat most values twice in a row.
scene_chest_table: Per-scene table of barrier tile and treasure chest placement data. Indexed by scene ID, each entry points to a variable-length list of 4-byte records: X tile, Y tile, content (item ID or tile index), flags (event flag ID, bit 7 = end sentinel). Most scenes point to $FF (no barriers/chests). Used by PlaceOpenedChestTiles (blocking tiles tied to event flags), HandleChestInteraction (treasure by player position), and radar_map_screen (transition markers on world map).
scene_warps: Master warp definition table — one of the largest structures in bank 1 (10 KB). Indexed by scene ID, each entry points to a variable-length list of warp-def entries containing two sub-structures: scene-warp (door/entrance warps with trigger rectangle, destination scene, destination coords, facing) and stair-warp (staircase warps with climb-animation offsets). Both sub-types use $FF as list terminator. The warps_interaction system checks player position against these rectangles each frame to trigger scene transitions.
shared_word_table: 15 item name prefix component strings used for compositional rendering. When the ConsoleStringRenderer encounters $10 InsertSharedWord, it indexes this table: 'Crystal ', 'Diamond ', 'Dark ', 'Hieroglyph ', 'Inca ', 'Mystery ', 'Prison ', 'Plate ', 'Psycho ', 'Restores ', etc. Shared prefixes reduce string storage.
signed_cosine_table_8bit: Full-cycle signed 8-bit cosine table — 256 entries, entry k = round(127 × cos(k × 1.40625°)): $7F at k=0, $00 at k=$40, $81 (−127) at k=$80, $00 at k=$C0. Because it starts at the 90° peak it is also the continuation of sine_table_8bit (sine index k+64). Used as the second axis of orbital motion with sine_table_8bit (ApplyOrbitalOffsetXY, ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef, the incan ruins whirligig).
sine_table_16bit: 16-bit high-precision sine table — 128 word entries covering one quarter-wave (0°–90°, 0.703125° per step): entry k ≈ 32767 × sin(k × 0.703125°), $0000 to $7FFD. Used by the Mode 7 perspective system for rotation matrix calculations, which index it up to 512 words so the read continues through cosine_table_16bit and neg_sine_halfwave_16bit (see the block note).
sine_table_8bit: 8-bit sine lookup table — 64 entries covering one quarter-wave (0°–90°). Values range $00 to $7F. Entry i = round(127 × sin(i × 1.40625°)). Consumers index it with the full 0–255 range; entries 64–255 are read from the adjacent signed_cosine_table_8bit (see the block note). Used by actor code for circular/oscillating motion (whirligig, skulker, sand fanger spiral attacks) and by scene_lifecycle for the screen-transition sine-wave effect. Also used by system_init as a known zero-byte source address (entry 0) for WRAM DMA clearing.
slope_curve_table:
209-byte table at the start of the block. Despite its name it is not a scene-flag table: system_core's init code points slopeCurvePtrA/B ($09BA/$09BC) at its start and decelCurvePtr ($09C2, also $09BE/$09C0/$09C4) at +$20. slope_ramp_physics reads 16-bit values from those pointers indexed by (step counter & $0F) × 2, so the first 64 bytes are two 16-word curves:
- $00–$1F: default slope acceleration curve — word $0001 at steps 0, 4, 8 and 12, otherwise $0000.
- $20–$3F: default deceleration curve — word $0001 at steps 7 and 15, otherwise $0000.

The remaining bytes have no reference by name in the extracted code: $42–$C0 is a stepped ramp ($01 ×8, $02 ×8, … up to $10 ×7) and $C1–$D0 counts $E0–$EF. Their consumer is unknown (logged as an open question).
will_ability_anim_table: Animation configuration for Will's 3 attack abilities. Each entry is a 6-byte record with sprite frame indices, hitbox dimensions, and timing data stored to climbStateData registers ($09E0/$09E2). Index 0 = Psycho Dash, 1 = Psycho Slider, 2 = Spin Dash. Referenced by LoadAbilityAnimTableA in attack_ability_system.asm.
